nodes.summary: The generator of the line-counting process of the ancestral selection graph with scaled selection coefficient `σ` (time in units of `2N` generations, the scaling of `generator`): from `n` lines, branching `n → n + 1` at rate `n σ` and coalescence `n → n - 1` at rate `C(n, 2)`.
nodes.title: Generator of the ancestral selection graph line-counting process

nodes.summary: Detailed balance of the ancestral-selection-graph chain: `π_k · (k σ) = π_{k+1} · C(k + 1, 2)` for every `k` (the flux `k → k + 1` equals the flux `k + 1 → k`). This is an identity for every real `σ`.
nodes.title: Detailed balance

nodes.summary: Global balance (stationarity `π Q = 0`) of the ancestral-selection-graph chain at state `k + 1`: the outflow `π_{k+1} ((k + 1) σ + C(k + 1, 2))` equals the inflow `π_k (k σ) + π_{k+2} C(k + 2, 2)` (for `k = 0` the inflow from the unreachable state `0` vanishes).
nodes.title: Global balance

nodes.summary: For `σ > 0` the stationary weights are nonnegative.
nodes.title: Stationary weights under selection are nonnegative

nodes.summary: The stationary law of the ancestral-selection-graph line-counting process with `σ > 0`: `π_k = (2σ)^k / k! / (e^{2σ} - 1)` for `k ≥ 1` and `π_0 = 0`, a Poisson`(2σ)` law conditioned to be positive. For `σ = 0` the stationary law is `δ₁`: branching vanishes, coalescence reaches state `1`, and state `1` is absorbing, so `π_1 = 1` and `π_k = 0` otherwise (the limit of the `σ > 0` formula as `σ → 0`).
nodes.title: Stationary law of the ancestral selection graph line counts

nodes.summary: The sojourn density conditioned on fixation, the Doob `h`-transform of the Green's function by the fixation probability `u`: `G(p, x) u(x) / u(p)` (Kimura–Ohta 1969; Ewens 2004, Chapter 4). At `p = 0` it is the junk value `0`.
nodes.title: Sojourn density conditioned on fixation

nodes.summary: The scale density is continuous on `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Continuity of the scale density on $(0, 1)$

nodes.summary: The scale function is continuous on `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Continuity of the scale function on $(0, 1)$

nodes.summary: The scale-function ratio `S / S(1)` solves the backward equation `a / 2 · u'' + b · u' = 0` on `(0, 1)`.
nodes.title: Kimura (1962)

nodes.summary: Let `g` be continuous on `(0, 1)` and assume the two halves of the Green integral are integrable away from the opposite boundary: `S g / (a ψ)` on `[0, q]` and `(S(1) - S) g / (a ψ)` on `[q, 1]` for every `q ∈ (0, 1)` (true for every `g` continuous on `[0, 1]` under genic selection, where `S / (a ψ)` is bounded near `0` and `(S(1) - S) / (a ψ)` near `1`). Then `v(q) = ∫₀¹ G(q, x) g(x) dx` solves `L v = -g` on…
nodes.title: Green's representation (Ewens 2004, Chapter 4; Karlin–Taylor 1981, Chapter 15)

nodes.summary: Under the hypotheses of `diffusionGenerator_integral_greenFunction` for `g = u` (the fixation probability), the function `w(q) = u(q) · ∫₀¹ G*(q, x) dx`, with `G*` the conditional sojourn density, solves `L w = -u` on `(0, 1)` (Ewens 2004, Chapter 4).
nodes.title: Conditional mean time to fixation, backward equation

nodes.summary: The general generator with drift `σ x (1 - x)` and variance `x (1 - x)` is the Wright–Fisher generator with genic selection.
nodes.title: Wright–Fisher generator with genic selection as a general diffusion

nodes.summary: The backward generator of a one-dimensional diffusion with drift `b` and infinitesimal variance `a`: `(L u)(x) = a(x) / 2 · u''(x) + b(x) · u'(x)`.
nodes.title: Backward generator of a one-dimensional diffusion

nodes.summary: The drift `2 c x (1 - x) (h + (1 - 2h) x)` of an allele at frequency `x` with genotype fitnesses `1`, `1 + h s`, `1 + s` (for zero, one and two copies), `c = N s`, time in units of `2N` generations (Kimura 1962). For `h = 1/2` it is genic selection with `σ = c`.
nodes.title: Drift of an allele under selection with dominance

nodes.summary: A function continuous on `[0, 1]`, differentiable on `(0, 1)` with derivative differentiable on `(0, 1)`, solving `L u = 0` on `(0, 1)` with `u(0) = 0` and `u(1) = 1` equals `S / S(1)` on `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the scale-function ratio (Kimura 1962)

nodes.summary: If `u` is continuous on `[0, 1]`, differentiable on `(0, 1)` with derivative differentiable on `(0, 1)`, and `L u = 0` on `(0, 1)`, then `u = u(0) + (u(1) - u(0)) · S / S(1)` on `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Solutions of `L u = 0`

nodes.summary: Two functions continuous on `[0, 1]`, differentiable on `(0, 1)` with derivatives differentiable on `(0, 1)`, with `L u = L v` on `(0, 1)` and the same values at `0` and `1`, agree on `[0, 1]`. Together with `diffusionGenerator_integral_greenFunction` this identifies the Green integral as the solution of `L v = -g`, `v(0) = v(1) = 0` whenever it has this regularity.
nodes.title: Uniqueness for the Dirichlet problem

nodes.summary: With `D = 2h - 1`, for `p ∈ [0, 1]`, `u(p) = ∫₀^p e^{-2cDx(1-x) - 2cx} dx / ∫₀¹ e^{-2cDx(1-x) - 2cx} dx`.
nodes.title: Kimura's scale-function ratio with dominance (Kimura 1962)

nodes.summary: The scale-function ratio lies in `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Dirichlet ratio lies in $(0, 1)$

nodes.summary: A fixed allele stays fixed.
nodes.title: Dirichlet ratio equals one at $p = 1$

nodes.summary: For genic selection the general scale-function ratio is `kimuraFixation σ p` on `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Kimura's formula as a corollary

nodes.summary: An absent allele is never fixed (for every `b`, `a`).
nodes.title: Dirichlet ratio vanishes at $p = 0$

nodes.summary: The analytic Dirichlet ratio `S(p) / S(1)` for drift `b` and variance `a` (Kimura 1962; Ewens 2004, Chapter 4). This is the solution of the backward boundary-value problem `L u = 0`, `u(0) = 0`, `u(1) = 1` (see `eq_fixationProb_of_diffusionGenerator_eq_zero`). It is the hitting probability `P_p(hit 1 before 0)` only when both boundaries are Feller-accessible; that is not implied by `IsRegularDiffusion` (see the…
nodes.title: Dirichlet ratio $S(p)/S(1)$ of the scale function

nodes.summary: The neutral conditional fixation time satisfies the conditioned backward equation `L_0 (p · t̄₁(p)) = -p` on `(0, 1)`.
nodes.title: Backward equation for the neutral conditional fixation time

nodes.summary: The selection duality in operator form: `L_σ` applied to `y ↦ (1 - y) ^ n` equals the ancestral-selection-graph generator applied to `k ↦ (1 - x) ^ k` at `n`.
nodes.title: Selection duality in operator form

nodes.summary: Selection duality (Mano 2009) at generator level, with the line-counting process of the ancestral selection graph (Krone–Neuhauser 1997) as the dual: the Wright–Fisher generator with genic selection maps `y ↦ (1 - y) ^ n` to `C(n, 2) ((1 - x)^(n-1) - (1 - x)^n) + n σ ((1 - x)^(n+1) - (1 - x)^n)`. This identity holds for every real `σ`; the dual is a Markov chain only for `σ ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Selection duality (Mano 2009)

nodes.summary: The general Green's function of the neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion (`b = 0`, `a = x (1 - x)`) is the neutral Green's function of `Sojourn.lean` for `x ∈ (0, 1)`.
nodes.title: General Green's function agrees with the neutral Wright–Fisher one

nodes.summary: The Green's function (analytic Green kernel) of `-L` with Dirichlet conditions at `0` and `1` (Ewens 2004, Chapter 4; Karlin–Taylor 1981, Chapter 15): `G(p, x) = 2 S(min p x) (S(1) - S(max p x)) / (S(1) a(x) ψ(x))`. In the diffusion reading (which requires Feller-accessible boundaries), `G(p, x) dx` is the expected time spent in `(x, x + dx)` before absorption.
nodes.title: Dirichlet Green's function of a one-dimensional diffusion

nodes.summary: `ψ' = -(2 b / a) ψ` inside the interval.
nodes.title: Derivative of the scale density

nodes.summary: `S' = ψ` inside the interval.
nodes.title: Derivative of the scale function is the scale density

nodes.summary: Loss probability from the stationary ancestral selection graph (Mano 2009): for `σ > 0`, `∑ₖ π_k (1 - x)^k = 1 - kimuraFixation σ x`, i.e. the loss probability of the favoured allele at frequency `x` is the probability that all lines of the stationary ancestral selection graph carry the unfavoured allele. Only the series identity is formalized; the sampling interpretation is not.
nodes.title: Loss probability from the stationary ancestral selection graph

nodes.summary: The neutral stationary law is `δ₁`: its generating function is `y`.
nodes.title: Neutral stationary law is the point mass at one

nodes.summary: The probability generating function of the stationary law: for `σ > 0` and every real `y`, `∑ₖ π_k y^k = (e^{2σy} - 1) / (e^{2σ} - 1)`.
nodes.title: Generating function of the stationary law under selection

nodes.summary: The neutral stationary weights sum to `1`.
nodes.title: Neutral stationary weights sum to one

nodes.summary: For `σ > 0` the stationary weights sum to `1`.
nodes.title: Stationary weights under selection sum to one

nodes.summary: For the neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion (`b = 0`, `a = x (1 - x)`) and `p ∈ (0, 1)`, the total conditional sojourn time `∫₀¹ G(p, x) u(x) / u(p) dx` is `-2 (1 - p) log (1 - p) / p`.
nodes.title: The general `h`-transform specializes to Kimura–Ohta

nodes.summary: Dirichlet condition at `1`: `∫₀¹ G(1, x) g(x) dx = 0` (for every `b`, `a`, `g`).
nodes.title: Dirichlet condition of the Green's function at one

nodes.summary: Dirichlet condition at `0`: `∫₀¹ G(0, x) g(x) dx = 0` (for every `b`, `a`, `g`).
nodes.title: Dirichlet condition of the Green's function at zero

nodes.summary: For `p ∈ (0, 1)`, `∫₀¹ G(p, x) · x / p dx = -2 (1 - p) log (1 - p) / p`, with `G` the neutral Green's function and `u(x) = x` the neutral fixation probability.
nodes.title: Neutral conditional fixation time as an `h`-transformed sojourn integral
Neutral conditional loss time

nodes.summary: The diffusion with dominance is regular.
nodes.title: Diffusion with dominance is regular

nodes.summary: The Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection is regular.
nodes.title: Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection is regular

nodes.summary: Regularity hypotheses for a diffusion on `(0, 1)` with drift `b` and variance `a`: `a` is positive and continuous on `(0, 1)`, `b / a` is continuous on `(0, 1)` and integrable on `[0, 1]` (so the scale function is finite up to both boundaries). The values of `b` and `a` at `0` and `1` are irrelevant. These are standing hypotheses for this file, not Feller's classification of regular boundaries: they do not imply…
nodes.title: Standing regularity hypotheses for a diffusion on $(0, 1)$

nodes.summary: For `p ∈ (0, 1)`, `p · t̄₁(p) + (1 - p) · t̄₀(p) = -2 (p log p + (1 - p) log (1 - p))`, the unconditional mean absorption time.
nodes.title: Total expectation

nodes.summary: The neutral conditional mean time to fixation `t̄₁(p) = -2 (1 - p) log (1 - p) / p`, in units of `2N` generations (Kimura–Ohta 1969). It is meaningful for `p ∈ (0, 1)`; at `p = 0` the division gives the junk value `0` (the limit is `2`, see `tendsto_neutralFixationTime_zero`).
nodes.title: Neutral conditional mean time to fixation

nodes.summary: Loss of an allele at frequency `p` is fixation of the other allele at `1 - p`.
nodes.title: Neutral loss time equals fixation time at $1 - p$

nodes.summary: The neutral conditional mean time to loss `t̄₀(p) = -2 p log p / (1 - p)`, in units of `2N` generations (Kimura–Ohta 1969). It is meaningful for `p ∈ (0, 1)`.
nodes.title: Neutral conditional mean time to loss

nodes.summary: The loss probability in Kimura's formula, written with positive exponents: for `σ ≠ 0`, `1 - kimuraFixation σ x = (e^{2σ(1 - x)} - 1) / (e^{2σ} - 1)`.
nodes.title: Loss probability in Kimura's fixation formula

nodes.summary: The scale density is positive.
nodes.title: Positivity of the scale density

nodes.summary: The scale density of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection is `e^{-2σy}` on `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Scale density of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection

nodes.summary: The scale density `ψ(y) = exp (-∫₀^y 2 b(z) / a(z) dz)` of the diffusion with drift `b` and variance `a` (Karlin–Taylor 1981, Chapter 15).
nodes.title: Scale density of a one-dimensional diffusion

nodes.summary: `S(1) > 0`, so the scale-function ratio and the Green's function have a positive denominator.
nodes.title: Scale function is positive at one

nodes.summary: The scale function vanishes at `0`.
nodes.title: Scale function vanishes at zero

nodes.summary: The scale function `S(p) = ∫₀^p ψ(y) dy`, normalized by `S(0) = 0`.
nodes.title: Scale function of a one-dimensional diffusion

nodes.summary: The scale function is strictly increasing on `[0, 1]`.
nodes.title: Scale function is strictly increasing

nodes.summary: A new neutral mutation that is destined to fix takes on average `2` units (`4N` generations) to do so (Kimura–Ohta 1969).
nodes.title: `t̄₁(0⁺) = 2`
